meta.title: Connect Email to ChatGPT: Any Mailbox Plugin Setup
meta.description: Give ChatGPT a real inbox: install Any Mailbox from the ChatGPT plugin directory, sign in to MCPEmails, pick your mailboxes. OAuth, no API key. One inbox free.

hero.lead: Install Any Mailbox, the MCPEmails plugin in the ChatGPT plugin directory, sign in, and ChatGPT can read, search, send, reply, forward, schedule and organize your real mail.
hero.answer: In ChatGPT, open Plugins, find Any Mailbox by MCPEmails in the plugin directory and click Install plugin, then Connect. Sign in to MCPEmails and choose which mailboxes ChatGPT can reach and how much access it gets. In a chat, type @ and pick Any Mailbox. Without the plugin, add a custom MCP server on chatgpt.com with the URL https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp and OAuth; that works on ChatGPT Go and paid plans.

method.title: How ChatGPT connects: OAuth, no API key
method.body: ChatGPT runs the standard MCP OAuth flow against this server. It registers itself with RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, so there is no client ID to create, and authorizes with authorization code plus PKCE using S256. No client secret is ever transmitted, and the token carries only the scopes you approve on our consent screen. The access token it receives lasts an hour and refreshes itself; it is listed in Dashboard, API Keys as OAuth: followed by the client name, which is where you revoke the connection.

setup.h: Create a free account and connect a mailbox
setup.p: Sign up at mcpemails.com, no card needed, and connect your mailbox under Dashboard, Inboxes. Outlook and Microsoft 365 connect with Sign in with Microsoft; Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo, Zoho and Yandex take an app-specific password; anything else connects over IMAP and SMTP. One inbox is free, forever.

setup.h: Install Any Mailbox from the plugin directory
setup.p: Any Mailbox is the plugin MCPEmails publishes in the ChatGPT plugin directory. In ChatGPT, open Plugins in the sidebar, find Any Mailbox (or open its listing, linked below), click Install plugin and then Connect. The directory is open on every ChatGPT plan, on the web, desktop and mobile.
ChatGPT sends you to MCPEmails. Sign in with the account that holds your mailboxes. If you are already signed in, you go straight to the consent screen.

setup.h: Choose mailboxes and access, then use it with @
setup.p: The consent screen asks how much access ChatGPT gets: Read-only, Standard, Full access, or Custom to pick permissions one by one. Choose All inboxes or Specific inboxes, then click Allow access. Back in ChatGPT, type @ in a chat and pick Any Mailbox, or just ask about your mail: ChatGPT uses installed plugins when they fit the request.

listingLink: Any Mailbox in the ChatGPT plugin directory

fallback.title: Add the same server as a custom MCP server
fallback.sub: If Any Mailbox is not available in your ChatGPT account or workspace, add MCPEmails as a custom MCP server instead. That works on chatgpt.com with ChatGPT Go and paid plans, and it reaches the same mailboxes.

steps.p: On chatgpt.com, open Plugins, then Personal, click Add at the top right and choose Add custom MCP server. This works on the web only: the mobile app cannot add one.
Name it MCPEmails and paste https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp under Connection.
Choose OAuth, tick I understand and want to continue, click Create as a plugin, then sign in with MCPEmails and approve the scopes you want ChatGPT to hold.
In a chat, type @ and pick MCPEmails. The pick applies to that message, so @mention it again when a follow-up needs your email.

gotchas.h: Install once, then make sure the chat is using it
gotchas.p: Any Mailbox installs from the plugin directory on every ChatGPT plan. On Business and Enterprise, an admin may need to make the plugin available for the workspace first. The custom MCP server, the fallback, is web-only and needs ChatGPT Go or a paid plan. In both cases the step people miss is in the chat: if ChatGPT answers without looking at your mail, type @ and pick Any Mailbox (or MCPEmails, for the custom server) so that message uses it.

gotchas.h: Pick OAuth, not no-authentication, when you create the custom server
gotchas.p: The custom-server form asks how to authenticate. This server refuses anonymous calls: an unauthenticated request gets a 401 carrying an OAuth discovery pointer, which is what a compliant client follows to start the flow. Choosing no authentication produces a connector that fails on its first tool call rather than at setup, which is the confusing way round. The plugin skips this question: it always signs in with OAuth.

gotchas.h: Read-only is a real option and often the right first one
gotchas.p: The consent screen lets you hand ChatGPT read:email and search:email alone. That is enough for triage, summarising and finding things, and it removes every irreversible action from the table while you decide how much further you want to go.

limits: Requests are rate limited per key in per-minute, hourly and daily windows sized to your plan. A 429 carries Retry-After.
The server is request and response only. There are no webhooks and no server-initiated events, so new mail never wakes your agent by itself. To react to arriving mail, poll on a schedule.

Mail is fetched live from your provider on every call and never stored. Only the encrypted OAuth token or app password is kept, so a revoked token or a changed mailbox password ends access immediately.

faq.q: Can ChatGPT read and send my email?
faq.a: Yes. Install Any Mailbox, the MCPEmails plugin in the ChatGPT plugin directory, or add MCPEmails as a custom MCP server. Either way ChatGPT gets tools for reading, searching, sending, replying, forwarding, organizing and scheduling mail, limited to the access you approve when you sign in.

faq.q: Is Any Mailbox the same as MCPEmails?
faq.a: Yes. Any Mailbox is the name MCPEmails has in the ChatGPT plugin directory, published by MCPEmails. It uses the same account, mailboxes and consent screen as a custom MCP server at https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp, so you need only one of the two.

faq.q: Why can I not add a custom MCP server in ChatGPT?
faq.a: Custom MCP servers can be added on Go and paid plans, on chatgpt.com: the mobile app does not offer it. On a Business or Enterprise workspace, an admin or owner may need to add it. The Any Mailbox plugin has none of these limits, so install it from the plugin directory instead. If MCPEmails is added but ChatGPT does not use it, type @ in the chat and pick it; the pick applies to one message at a time.

faq.q: Do I need an API key for ChatGPT?
faq.a: No. The plugin signs in with OAuth, and so does a custom MCP server when you pick OAuth: ChatGPT registers itself and completes an authorization code plus PKCE flow. API keys are for clients that cannot do that, and for scripts.

faq.q: Which mailboxes can ChatGPT reach this way?
faq.a: Outlook.com and Microsoft 365 over Sign in with Microsoft, where a work account may need an IT admin to approve the app once; Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo, Zoho and Yandex with an app-specific password; and any other mailbox that speaks IMAP and SMTP on the standard ports. The client sees them all through the same connection: your agent calls inbox_list first to discover every connected mailbox and its id, so there are no UUIDs to paste anywhere.

faq.q: Can ChatGPT send email without me seeing it?
faq.a: Only if you let it. Sending is gated on the send:email scope, so a key or a token without that scope cannot send at all. On top of that, an inbox owner can require human approval in the dashboard, which holds every send, reply, forward, draft send and scheduled send until a person releases it.

faq.q: Is my email stored on your servers?
faq.a: No. Every message is fetched live from your provider for the request that asked for it and handed straight to your client. Only the encrypted OAuth token or app password is kept, so future calls can authenticate. Deleting the inbox in the dashboard, or revoking access at your provider, ends the connection at once.
